title: Body Fat Calculator
description: Estimate your body fat percentage using the U.S. Navy circumference method with a measuring tape.

fields.label: Hip circumference (women only)
fields.helpText: Only used when Sex is set to Female.

formula.summary: The U.S. Navy method estimates body fat from simple tape-measure circumferences, using a formula validated against underwater weighing.

faqs.question: How accurate is the tape-measure method?
faqs.answer: It's typically within 3-4 percentage points of more precise lab methods like DEXA scans - accurate enough to track trends over time, but not a clinical-grade measurement.

faqs.question: Where exactly should I measure?
faqs.answer: Neck: just below the larynx. Waist: at the navel for men, at the narrowest point for women. Hip (women): at the widest point of the hips. Measure snugly but without compressing the skin.

faqs.question: Why does the formula need hip measurement for women only?
faqs.answer: The U.S. Navy method uses sex-specific formulas because body fat distribution differs by sex on average - the women's formula was calibrated using hip circumference as an additional predictor for better accuracy.

seoContent.heading: Why body fat percentage matters more than weight alone
seoContent.body: Two people with the same weight and height can have very different body compositions - one could carry mostly muscle, the other mostly fat. Body fat percentage gives a clearer picture of health and fitness than weight or BMI alone, since it directly reflects how much of your body is fat tissue versus lean mass.

seoContent.heading: About the U.S. Navy circumference method
seoContent.body: Developed for military fitness assessments, this method uses only a measuring tape and a small number of circumference measurements, making it far more accessible than skinfold calipers or lab-based methods like DEXA or hydrostatic weighing, while still providing a reasonably reliable estimate for tracking change over time.
